name: Couscous Bel Merga Hamra (Couscous in Red Sauce)
description: Steamed couscous served with a tomato-red sauce of chicken, chickpeas and a few simple vegetables: the everyday Friday-lunch version of the national dish.

steps.text: Heat the oil in the base of a couscoussier or a large pot. Brown the chicken for 5 minutes, then add the onions, paprika, pepper and cinnamon and cook until the onions soften.
Stir in the tomato paste and grated tomatoes, add the chickpeas, salt and water, and bring to a boil.
Moisten the couscous with salted water, rub it with your fingers to break lumps, and steam it in the top part for 20 minutes over the simmering sauce.
Add the carrots to the sauce, tip the couscous into a wide dish, sprinkle with a little cold salted water, break up lumps and steam it again for 15 minutes.
Add the courgettes to the sauce and simmer for 15 minutes, until the chicken and vegetables are tender.
Work the butter into the hot couscous, mound it on a platter, make a well and ladle over some sauce. Serve the rest of the chicken, vegetables and sauce alongside, with harissa.

tips: Steaming the couscous twice makes it light; do not skip the second steam.
Leave the sauce a little thin: the couscous drinks it up.

name: Couscous Bel Merga Beida (Couscous in White Sauce)
description: A pale, gently spiced couscous with chicken, chickpeas and turnips in a clear onion broth, with sweet raisin onions sometimes spooned on top.

steps.text: Heat the oil in the couscoussier pot, add the chicken, onions, cinnamon, pepper and salt and cook without browning for 5 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and water, bring to a boil and skim, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Moisten the couscous with salted water, rub it loose and steam it over the pot for 20 minutes.
Add the turnips and carrots to the broth. Re-wet and break up the couscous and steam it again for 15 minutes.
Add the courgettes and cook for 15 minutes more until everything is tender.

Mix the butter into the couscous and mound it on a dish. Drain a ladle of onions and chickpeas, simmer them with the raisins and sugar for 5 minutes, and spoon over the top. Serve with the broth and vegetables.

tips: The sauce stays white because the chicken is not browned and no paprika or tomato goes in.

name: Couscous Bel Guedid (Couscous with Dried Meat)
description: A festive couscous in which guedid, sun-dried and preserved meat, is simmered until tender in a rich sauce with chickpeas and vegetables.

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: go lightly, the meat is salty

steps.text: Soak the guedid in warm water for 30 minutes, then rinse and cut it into pieces.
Fry the chopped onions in the oil in the couscoussier pot, add the guedid, paprika, pepper and tomato paste and stir for 5 minutes.
Add the soaked chickpeas and water and simmer, covered, for 1 hour until the meat starts to soften.
Steam the moistened couscous in the top part for 20 minutes.
Add the carrots and turnips to the pot, re-wet and break up the couscous, steam again for 15 minutes.
Add the courgettes and cook 15 minutes more, tasting for salt only at the end.
Work the smen into the couscous, mound it, and serve the guedid and vegetables over it with the sauce.

tips: Guedid is salty: soak well and add salt only at the end.
If you cannot find guedid, use salted and sun-dried beef from a halal butcher.

name: Mqarna Bel Marqa (Macaroni in Meat Sauce)
description: A weeknight classic: macaroni tossed in a savoury tomato and minced-beef sauce with a little cinnamon.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the beef and brown it for 8 minutes, breaking up lumps.
Stir in the garlic, paprika, cinnamon, pepper and tomato paste, then the tomatoes, salt and water. Simmer 20 minutes until thick.
Meanwhile boil the macaroni in plenty of salted water until just tender and drain.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and let it sit, covered, for 5 minutes. Serve with grated cheese if you like.

tips: A splash of the pasta water loosens the sauce if it gets too thick.

name: Spaghetti Bel Kefta (Spaghetti with Spiced Meatballs)
description: Spaghetti with small coriander-and-cumin meatballs in a smooth tomato sauce, the Algerian family take on a pasta and meatball plate.

steps.text: Mix the beef with half the onion, one crushed garlic clove, parsley, cumin, half the paprika, egg, breadcrumbs, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Roll into walnut-sized balls.
Brown the meatballs in 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan for 6 minutes, turning, then set aside.
In the same pan fry the remaining onion and garlic in the remaining oil for 4 minutes, add the paprika, tomato paste, tomatoes, salt and 200 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the meatballs to the sauce and cook for 12 minutes.
Boil the spaghetti until al dente, drain, and serve topped with the meatballs and sauce.

tips: Wet hands make the meatballs easier to roll.

name: Spaghetti Bel Sardine (Spaghetti with Sardines)
description: A coastal budget supper: spaghetti tossed with sardines, garlic, tomato and a hint of chilli and lemon.

steps.text: Heat the oil, soften the garlic for 1 minute, then add the paprika, cumin, tomato paste and tomatoes with the salt and cook for 10 minutes until saucy.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water until al dente; drain, keeping a ladle of cooking water.
Lay the sardine fillets in the sauce and cook gently for 5 minutes, breaking them up as you stir.
Toss in the spaghetti with a splash of its water, the parsley, chilli and lemon juice and serve at once.

tips: Canned sardines in oil work well too: drain and add them for the last 2 minutes.

name: Riz Bel Djaj (Rice with Chicken)
description: Fragrant long-grain rice cooked with golden chicken pieces, onion, peas and a pinch of turmeric.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 8 minutes, add the onion and spices and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the water and salt, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is nearly cooked.
Rinse the rice, add it with the peas and carrot, stir once, cover and cook on low heat until the water is absorbed.
Rest, covered, for 10 minutes and fluff with a fork.

tips: Do not stir again after adding rice or it turns sticky.

name: Riz Bel Khodra (Rice with Vegetables)
description: A bright pilaf of rice with carrots, peas, courgette and peppers, an easy vegan side or light main.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 4 minutes, add the carrots and pepper and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, salt and pepper, then add the courgette and peas. Cook 3 minutes.
Add the washed rice and water, bring to a boil, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes, then fluff and serve.

name: Riz Bel Thon (Rice with Tuna)
description: A pantry supper of rice with tuna, tomato and sweetcorn.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add tomato paste and paprika and cook 1 minute.
Add rice, salt and water, cover and cook on low heat for 15 minutes.
Fold in the tuna and sweetcorn, cover for 5 minutes, add lemon juice and fluff.

name: Gratin de Macaroni (Baked Pasta Gratin)
description: Macaroni and minced beef under a golden béchamel and cheese crust, a party-table favourite.

steps.text: Boil the macaroni 2 minutes short of the pack time and drain.
Brown the onion and beef in the oil for 10 minutes with the tomato paste, half the salt and the pepper.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and cook until thick, then add nutmeg, remaining salt and half the cheese.
Mix pasta, meat and a third of the sauce in a baking dish, spread the rest of the sauce on top, scatter cheese, and bake at 200 C until golden.

tips: Rest 5 minutes before slicing so it holds together.

name: Gratin de Batata (Potato Gratin)
description: Thin potato slices baked in a garlicky creamy milk with melted cheese until bubbling.

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and slice them 3 mm thick. Rub a baking dish with butter.
Warm the milk and cream with garlic, salt, pepper and nutmeg for 3 minutes.
Layer potatoes with half the cheese and pour over the milk mix. Cover with foil and bake at 190 C for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil, add the remaining cheese and bake 20 minutes more until golden and tender.

name: Batata Mahchiya (Stuffed Potatoes in Tomato Sauce)
description: Potato halves hollowed and filled with spiced minced beef, then simmered in a light tomato sauce.

steps.text: Cut a slice off each potato's end so it stands, and scoop out the middle with a spoon, leaving a 1 cm wall.
Mix the beef with one grated onion, parsley, half the garlic, egg, spices and 1 tsp salt. Pack into the potatoes.
Fry the second onion and remaining garlic in oil for 4 minutes, add tomato paste, tomatoes and water and bring to a simmer.
Settle the potatoes in the sauce, cover and cook on low heat for 40 minutes, until fork tender.

tips: Save the scooped potato for soup or mash.

name: Batata Bel Marqa (Potatoes in Light Meat Sauce)
description: A comforting everyday stew of potatoes and beef in a light, lightly peppery onion and tomato sauce.

steps.text: Brown the beef with the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, add garlic, paprika, pepper and tomato paste.
Pour in the water, add salt, cover and cook for 30 minutes until the beef softens.
Add the potatoes and cook for 20 minutes until tender and the sauce is a little thick.
Scatter parsley and serve with bread.

name: Chtitha Sardine (Sardines in Spicy Red Sauce)
description: Fresh sardines poached in a spicy garlic, tomato and cumin sauce, served with bread to mop it up.

steps.text: Cook garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add paprika, cumin, harissa, tomato paste and tomatoes and simmer 12 minutes.
Add water and salt, lay in the sardines and cook gently for 8 minutes without stirring.
Garnish with coriander and serve with bread.

tips: Shake the pan instead of stirring so the sardines stay whole.

name: Adas Bel Marqa (Lentil Stew)
description: Brown lentils simmered with garlic, tomato and cumin into a thick, soothing stew.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add garlic, tomato paste and spices for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, carrot, water and salt. Boil, then simmer 30 minutes until the lentils collapse.
Stir in coriander and serve with bread and lemon.

name: Jelbana Bel Lham (Peas with Beef)
description: Tender green peas and carrots slowly stewed with beef in a light sauce.

steps.text: Brown the beef and onion in the oil for 8 minutes with the paprika, pepper and tomato paste.
Add water and salt, cover and cook for 30 minutes.
Add the carrots and peas and cook 15 minutes until soft and the sauce is silky.
Finish with parsley and serve with bread.

description: Chicken and peas in a gently spiced white-and-gold sauce with a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Cook the chicken with onion, oil, turmeric and pepper for 8 minutes without browning too hard.
Add water and salt and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Add the peas and cook 12 minutes until tender.
Stir in lemon juice and coriander and serve.

name: Loubia Khadra Bel Marqa (Green Beans in Sauce)
description: Green beans simmered with a little beef and tomato until silky and savoury.

steps.text: Brown the beef and onion in the oil for 8 minutes, add garlic, paprika, tomato paste and tomatoes.
Add the water and salt and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the beans and cook 15 minutes until very tender.

tips: Without meat, it is a simple vegan dish: add 1 tbsp more oil.
